newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP says coal, iron ore output rises.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP says coal, iron ore output rises.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Tuesday that its coal production rose 10 percent to 17.131 million tonnes in the nine months to February, while iron ore output rose five percent to 39.045 million tonnes.
The coal figures represent production from Queensland while the iron ore figures are for output from Western Australia.

Total production of coal for the nine months, including output from the United States, Indonesia and New South Wales, was 36.320 million tonnes, up from 34.547 million tonnes a year earlier. Coal production for the month of February totalled 3.885 million tonnes, up from 3.719 million a year earlier.
Iron ore production from Western Australian mines totalled 3.597 million tonnes for the month, down from 3.823 million a year earlier.
BHP said production of coal in Queensland was lower for February compared to a year earlier due mainly due to wet weather.
"Production of Queensland coal on a year to date basis was higher as a result of improved recovery and quality of feed ore combined with greater truck availability," BHP said.
It said production of coal in the United States was higher due to increased ore exposure.
"Lower coal shipments for February reflect lower demand for Queensland coal during the month partly offset by increased customer demand at New Mexico operations," the company said.
"Production of iron ore in Western Australia was lower for February due to heavy rain," BHP said.
"Higher shipments of Western Australian iron ore for February reflect increased customer demand in Japan and Korea for Yandi product," the company said.
